terms.meaning: Asking a focused question, doing an experiment carefully, watching closely and explaining what happened.
An experiment in which only one thing is changed at a time and everything else stays the same.
Noting carefully what you see and sense, and keeping a record of it.

items.name: Start from a simple wonder
items.formula: Turn something you notice into a clear question.
items.example: "Why does a puri puff up in hot oil?"

items.name: Things you could change
items.formula: List them first, such as thickness, flour, oil temperature and the way of dropping it in.
items.example: Try thick and thin dough with the same oil.

items.name: Change one thing at a time
items.formula: Keep all other conditions the same, or you cannot tell what caused the result.
items.example: To test thickness, use the same flour, oil and way of dropping.

items.name: Keep notes
items.formula: Write down everything you see, hear and smell.
items.example: Did the oil splatter? Did it smoke?

items.name: One round leads to more questions
items.formula: Results raise new questions to test.
items.example: Do puris puff better from fresh dough or stored dough?

mistakes.text: Changing two things at once does not tell you which one made the difference.
Science has not explained everything. Even why a puri swells is not fully understood.
